title: Setting Standards for Next Generation Active Copper Cables: Semtech Co-Chairs the New ACC MSA
summary: Semtech co-chairs the Active Copper Cable (ACC) MSA, defining open industry standards for next-gen copper interconnects that power AI data center growth.
body_markdown:
AI clusters are packing more compute into every rack, and every link between those racks adds to your power, cost and cable bulk. If you design or run a data center, you need short-reach interconnects that go farther than passive copper without the power draw of DSP-based cables.


Active copper cables (ACCs) with linear equalizers are built for those links. But without shared specifications, mixing cable and equipment vendors adds integration risk. That is why 13 companies launched the Active Copper Cable Multi-Source Agreement (ACC-MSA) on Feb. 23, 2026. Semtech co-chairs the group with MACOM, so the specifications draw on real ACC design experience.


##


What Is the ACC MSA?


The ACC MSA is an industry consortium dedicated to developing open, multi-vendor specifications for ACCs and the networking equipment that uses them. The founding membership represents a who's who of the industry: AMD, Amphenol, Ciena, Cisco, Dell Technologies, Keysight Technologies, Luxshare Technologies, MACOM, Molex, Multilane, NVIDIA, Semtech Corporation, and TE Connectivity.


The initial focus is on copper interconnects that integrate linear equalizers into copper cables — a key architectural choice that sets ACCs apart from conventional Digital Signal Processing (DSP)-based Active Electrical Cables (AECs). The consortium will define electrical, firmware and compliance test requirements to ensure seamless interoperability across networking equipment and cable vendors.


The goal is straightforward: create a multi-source ecosystem that lowers deployment risk, reduces cost and accelerates the industry-wide adoption of[next-generation copper solutions](https://blog.semtech.com/ofc-2026-semtech-advances-the-future-of-ai-data-center-optical-and-active-copper-interconnects) .


## Why Does Active Copper Cable Technology Matter for AI Data Centers?


AI infrastructure is driving an extraordinary buildout across global data centers. According to Alan Weckel, founder and technology analyst at 650 Group, AI hardware infrastructure spending is projected to exceed $1 trillion by 2029, with networking infrastructure alone approaching $200 billion in that timeframe. ACCs are emerging as a key enabling technology for these deployments — delivering the low-power, low-latency, short-reach interconnect performance that dense AI cluster architectures demand.


Active copper cables have already seen widespread industry deployment. The goal of the MSA specification effort is to define common standards to ensure interoperability across hardware platforms, rack designs and cable vendors.


"The ACC MSA is focused on driving innovation and collaboration," said Scott Schube, vice president of applications and product definition, signal integrity products at Semtech. "By creating a multi-source ecosystem, we aim to improve interconnect economics and speed industry-wide adoption of next-generation copper connectivity."


## Active Copper Cable Leadership: Deep Expertise, Industry Impact


Semtech serves as co-chair and technical specifications editor of the ACC MSA. These roles are a natural extension of the deep technical investment the company has made in active copper cable technology over the past several years.


The Semtech[CopperEdge™](https://www.semtech.com/technology/copperedge) product portfolio is purpose-built for ACC applications. The portfolio's linear equalizer/redriver integrated circuits (ICs) — spanning the GN8112, GN8214, GN8224, and GN8234 — are designed to extend copper cable reach well beyond the limits of passive Direct Attach Copper (DAC) cables, while consuming a fraction of the power required by DSP-based alternatives. For 800G and 1.6T data center deployments, the CopperEdge portfolio delivers extended reach at 112G and 224G per lane, ultra-low latency under 100 picoseconds, and power consumption up to 10 times lower than competing DSP-based solutions.


This technology has already seen significant commercial momentum. Semtech has collaborated with multiple leading interconnect manufacturers, including Amphenol Communications Solutions, Luxshare-Tech, Molex, TE Connectivity, and others —[to bring 1.6T octal small form-factor pluggable (OSFP) ACC products to market](https://www.semtech.com/company/press/copperedge-portfolio-low-power-800g-ai-data-centers) . These solutions are designed for the switch-to-server and rack-to-rack connectivity demands of next-generation AI/machine learning (ML) clusters, where power efficiency, bandwidth density and signal integrity are equally critical.


## How Do Linear Equalizers Improve Active Copper Cable Performance?


At the heart of the ACC MSA's technical vision is the integration of linear equalizers within the ends of copper cables. Unlike DSP-based alternatives, linear equalizers work by amplifying and reshaping signals in the analog domain — a simpler, lower-latency and more power-efficient approach for short-reach links where the channel is predictable and well-characterized.


This architecture enables ACCs to significantly extend the reach of copper cabling, reduce cable thickness and weight and maintain full compatibility with existing pluggable interfaces used by passive copper and optical interconnects. For data center operators, this translates to a clear upgrade path that preserves existing infrastructure investments while supporting the move to 800G and 1.6T network fabrics.


The ACC MSA's specifications will formalize these advantages into a common technical framework, ensuring that ACCs from different vendors work seamlessly together and giving data center operators the confidence to deploy at scale.


## What Comes Next for the ACC MSA?


With its founding members now aligned, the ACC MSA will draft and publish interoperability specifications. As co-chair, Semtech is playing an active role in shaping those standards, drawing on the real-world design experience gained through its CopperEdge product development and its ecosystem partnerships with leading cable manufacturers.


This consortium represents more than a standards effort. It reflects the industry's collective recognition that active copper cable technology is ready to take its place as a foundational component of AI-era data center infrastructure.


For more information on the ACC MSA, visit[acc-msa.org](https://www.acc-msa.org/) . To learn more about the Semtech CopperEdge technology for ACC and on-board applications, visit[semtech.com/technology/copperedge](https://www.semtech.com/technology/copperedge) .


## ACC MSA: Frequently Asked Questions


### What does "MSA" stand for in ACC MSA?


MSA stands for Multi-Source Agreement — an industry term for a consortium that defines shared technical specifications, so multiple vendors can produce interoperable products.


### What is the difference between an ACC and a DAC cable?


A DAC (Direct Attach Copper) cable is passive, limiting it to shorter reaches at high data rates. An ACC adds a linear equalizer to the cable assembly, extending reach and preserving signal integrity at rates a passive DAC cannot support.


### Will products built to the ACC MSA specifications work across different vendors?


That is the specific goal of the consortium. Once published, the ACC MSA specifications will define shared electrical, firmware and test requirements so ACCs and networking equipment from different member companies interoperate reliably.


### What data rates does the Semtech CopperEdge portfolio support today?


CopperEdge ICs currently support 112G and 224G per lane, enabling ACC and on-board applications from 400G up through 1.6T, ahead of the ACC MSA's forthcoming specifications.


### How can a company get involved with the ACC MSA?


Companies interested in participating can find membership information at acc-msa.org.


### When will the ACC MSA publish its first specifications?


No timeline has been announced. The consortium is currently in the drafting phase following its Feb. 23, 2026, launch, with Semtech contributing as co-chair and technical specifications editor.
